Now I see! The `opt_error` calls at lines 747, 753, 1205, 1208, 1247 are called during `opt_loop` → `opt_blks` → `opt_blk` → `opt_stmt`. These are called when the optimizer encounters division by zero or shift by more than 31 bits during constant folding.

When `opt_error` is called during `opt_loop`, it longjmps to `bpf_optimize`, which calls `opt_cleanup`. But `opt_init` completed successfully, so all pointers are valid. This is a clean path - no double-free.

Wait, but the description says the double-free is in `opt_cleanup`. Let me re-read the description more carefully.

Let me look at the `opt_init` function again. When `opt_init` fails partway through, it frees some pointers and then calls `opt_error`. But `opt_error` longjmps, so the freed pointers are never set to NULL. Then `opt_cleanup` frees them again.
